questions.q: Why is Receivables described as a subledger rather than the General Ledger itself?
options: Because it cannot generate any accounting entries at all
Because it captures detailed, transaction-level activity that gets summarized into journal entries before reaching the GL
Because it only tracks miscellaneous receipts
Because it replaces the need for a chart of accounts
questions.explain: Receivables holds full transaction-level detail, and Subledger Accounting summarizes that detail into journal entries that ultimately post to the General Ledger.

questions.q: What is the typical accounting entry for a standard invoice?
options: Debit Cash, credit Accounts Receivable
Debit Revenue, credit Accounts Receivable
Debit Accounts Receivable, credit Cash
Debit Accounts Receivable, credit Revenue
questions.explain: A standard invoice typically debits Accounts Receivable, increasing what the customer owes, and credits Revenue, recognizing the sale.

questions.q: What is the typical accounting entry for a standard receipt?
options: Debit Accounts Receivable, credit Revenue
Debit Revenue, credit Cash
Debit Accounts Receivable, credit Cash
Debit Cash, credit Accounts Receivable
questions.explain: A standard receipt is the mirror image of an invoice: it debits Cash and credits Accounts Receivable, reducing what the customer owes.

options: A manual process where a clerk types in GL account numbers on every transaction
A rules engine, configured during setup, that automatically derives the correct GL accounts based on transaction attributes
A feature that automatically reverses incorrect receipts
A report that lists every open transaction by aging bucket
questions.explain: AutoAccounting is configured once and automatically determines the correct GL account segment values based on attributes like transaction type, activity, or customer.

questions.q: On a miscellaneous receipt, what does Receivables credit instead of Accounts Receivable?
options: Nothing — the entry is debit only
Always the Revenue account
Always the Cash account
Whatever GL account the Receivables Activity of type Miscellaneous Cash specifies
questions.explain: Since a miscellaneous receipt has no customer balance to reduce, the credit side goes to the GL account defined on its Receivables Activity instead of Accounts Receivable.
